# Rosemary West

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c13 P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c34 P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** music teacher  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c4 P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v5 c4 P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosemary is a pretty, tall, fair, and placid woman. She has golden hair described as the color of new molasses taffy, which she wears in sleek, close coils, along with large, tranquil blue eyes, a high white forehead, and a finely shaped face. She dresses prettily and possesses a slow, sweet smile.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063), [v5 c4 P52](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0052), [v5 c13 P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007), [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c14 P39](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0039)_

## Personality

Rosemary is sweet, charming, delightful, and full of gracious friendliness. She is sympathetic, open-minded, and understanding, showing compassion toward others even in embarrassing situations. Though gentle and soft-spoken, she carries deep quiet passions and stays loyal to her commitments and old memories.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P65](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0065), [v5 c12 P5](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0005), [v5 c12 P18](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0018), [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c17 P78](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0078), [v5 c17 P81](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0081), [v5 c20 P20](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0020)_

- to be a friend, helper, and older sister to the Meredith children  <sub>[v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)</sub>

## History

When Rosemary was seventeen, she became engaged to Martin Crawford by a hidden spring in Rainbow Valley, but he drowned shortly after when his ship was wrecked. Following her mother's death and her sister Ellen's disappointment in love, Rosemary agreed to a solemn vow over her mother's Bible that neither sister would ever marry or part. She spent years living quietly with Ellen, giving music lessons to local children like Di and Nan Blythe because she enjoyed it. When John Meredith moved to the Glen, he met Rosemary and was struck by her beauty and charm, eventually falling deeply in love with her and proposing marriage. Bound by her vow to Ellen, Rosemary painfully wrote him a stiff, cool refusal to turn him away, leaving both of them heartbroken. Months later, after a visit to Kingsport, Una Meredith came to Rosemary in secret to ask her to marry her father, revealing that Mr. Meredith still loved her intensely. Rosemary welcomed Una as a friend and helper, realizing she could find happiness with John while offering love and support to his children.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c4 P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 c13 P0](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0000), [v5 c13 P6](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0006), [v5 c13 P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007), [v5 c21 P0](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0000), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024), [v5 c22 P41](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0041), [v5 c26 P15](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0015), [v5 c34 P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006), [v5 c34 P23](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0023), [v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)_

## Quotes

> Will you let me have it? You made it so knackily. I never saw anyone make a birch cup so since my little brother used to make them long ago—before he died.  <sub>[v5 c13 P15](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0015)</sub>

> I went to school with him—he was a Glen boy, you know—and he was a most detestable little prig even then. Oh, how we girls used to hate holding his fat, clammy hands in the ring-around games. But we must remember, dear, that he didn’t know that Adam had been a pet of yours. He thought he was just a common rooster. We must be just, even when we are terribly hurt.  <sub>[v5 c20 P20](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0020)</sub>

> I would never dream of trying to turn your father against you. I would love you all dearly. I don’t want to take your own mother’s place—she must always have that in your hearts. But neither have I any intention of being a stepmother. I want to be your friend and helper and chum. Don’t you think that would be nice, Una—if you and Faith and Carl and Jerry could just think of me as a good jolly chum—a big older sister?  <sub>[v5 c34 P31](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0031)</sub>
